## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: "Articles will be subject to a double-blind peer review process", with all documents visible to reviewers anonymous, including supplementary files and file properties (guidelines, https://web.archive.org/web/20250918094256/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions, copy dated 2025-09-18). The why-submit page promises "a detailed, double-blind review process" with an explanation of the basis for the decision (copy dated 2025-07-02). Before review the editors decide scope and standards (see Desk Rejection Rate) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. The guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18 contains no transfer, cascade or referral wording (searched: 0 hits outside HTML comments) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found on the pages read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev (35 reviews): 1.6 review rounds on average and 2.8 review reports on average (https://scirev.org/journal/european-sociological-review/, retrieved 2026-11-23). No journal-reported figure found |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source read. The guidelines say reviewers "will routinely be asked to comment" on whether a manuscript over 8,000 words has enough weight to justify its length (copy dated 2025-09-18) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific text found. The live guidelines (read in a real browser 2026-11-24, https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions) have no section on AI use or disclosure (searched the page text for "Policy on AI", "Disclosure of AI" and "generative": none), unlike the guidelines of other OUP titles. They mention that manuscripts may be screened, including by third-party services, for integrity issues such as image alteration and papermill activity, and offer an optional free Paperpal Preflight technical check. The publisher-wide OUP journals policy applies (see Summary) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate. Under the OUP journals policy (read in a real browser 2026-11-24) authors assert on submission that they followed it, and disclosure is required for the uses it lists |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 4 (this entry's own reading of the OUP journals policy): language polishing and reference formatting need no disclosure; editing, translation, data work, code and illustrative images are allowed with disclosure; presenting AI output as human research data is not allowed |
| **Summary** | OUP publication-ethics page (copy dated 2024-10-01): AI tools such as ChatGPT do not qualify as authors and OUP screens author lists for them; use of AI to help generate content or images, write code, process data or translate must be disclosed both in the cover letter and in the Methods or Acknowledgements section. That is the older copy. The current OUP Policy on AI Use & Disclosure for OUP Journals Authors (https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/preparing-and-submitting-your-manuscript/ai-principles-for-oxford-journals/policy-on-ai-use-and-disclosure-for-oxford-journals-authors, dated 13 July 2026, read in a real browser 2026-11-24) says: no disclosure needed for language polishing or reference formatting; disclosure needed for substantial editing, translation, data work, code and illustrative images, in the cover letter and the Acknowledgements (and the Methods where AI was integral), at submission and again on revision, with tool name and version, how it was used and the author's role in checking it; failure to disclose may be grounds for rejection; where a journal's own guidance varies, the journal's guidance wins (ESR's page states none) |
| **Source URL** | https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/preparing-and-submitting-your-manuscript/ai-principles-for-oxford-journals/policy-on-ai-use-and-disclosure-for-oxford-journals-authors (OUP policy, live); https://web.archive.org/web/20241001130642/https://academic.oup.com/pages/authoring/journals/preparing_your_manuscript/ethics (older OUP copy, 2024-10-01); https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions (journal guidelines, live, no AI text) |

### Preprint Policy

> Publisher-level policy, OUP author self-archiving page, copy dated 2026-11-02: https://web.archive.org/web/20261102215712/https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b. It says policies and embargo periods can differ by journal. The ESR guidelines page itself says nothing about preprints (searched, 0 hits).

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The "Author's Original Version", the un-refereed pre-submission version also called the preprint, may be posted anywhere at any time, on condition that after acceptance the author adds a statement that the article has been accepted by the journal |
| Under review | Yes, with a caveat | The same rule covers the version completed before submission. The journal asks for anonymised manuscripts, and a posted preprint can reveal authorship; the pages do not address this |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | Accepted manuscript: immediately on the author's personal webpage; in an institutional or non-commercial repository only after the embargo. Embargo: 12 months (OUP embargo list, https://academic.oup.com/pages/open-research/open-access/charges-licences-and-self-archiving/accepted-manuscript-embargo-periods, read in a real browser 2026-11-24). Not on commercial sites or repositories |
| Version of Record | No, unless open access | The published version may not be deposited in repositories or on third-party sites unless published under an open-access licence; private sharing within an institution or through STM-signatory collaboration networks is allowed |

## Format

> Source: ESR general instructions, Wayback copy dated 2025-09-18, https://web.archive.org/web/20250918094256/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions. HTML comments in the page were excluded. Anything newer is unverified.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original research articles in all fields of sociology; Data Brief manuscripts (a regular section describing data sources, design, sampling or questionnaire content, "standard article length"); Comments and Replies, which need not first be sent to the article authors (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18) |
| **Word limit** | "Usually around 8,000 words, including endnotes and references, but excluding tables and figures"; the journal will publish longer articles, in which case reviewers "will routinely be asked" whether the contribution justifies the length (same copy). No limit for Comments and Replies stated |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Partly. Over-length is allowed but triggers the reviewer question above; no exception procedure stated |
| **Abstract limit** | An abstract of not more than 200 words, plus keywords, a cover letter and a 50 to 100 word biography of each author (same copy) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 8,000 words. Author-date in-text citations in parentheses, alphabetical list; own work must be cited in a way that does not identify the author and references must not be redacted ("Author A" style is discouraged) |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed and peer reviewed: supplementary tables, figures and explanations as a single PDF, anonymous; replication material as a single zip uploaded at submission is encouraged (same copy). Tables and figures in the main text should be restricted to essential information |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figures at 1200 dpi for line drawings and 300 dpi for colour and half-tone, supplied separately after conditional acceptance; alt text is encouraged |
| **Style / submission format** | Format-free submission at first submission (a single PDF or Word file is "usually reliable"); English only ("acceptable English"; language editing optional); the manuscript-preparation section asks for double-spaced text with ample margins, serial page numbers and no more than two levels of subheadings; editable files (doc, docx, rtf or tex) are requested after acceptance; submission through ScholarOne (why-submit page copy dated 2025-07-02) |

### Orientation

> Counts come from Crossref records of the journal dated 2021-01-05 to 2026-11-19: 382 journal-article records, 356 with an abstract (93.2%). A record counts when its title or abstract matches the regular expression listed in the AI-Research Notes (case-insensitive, word-bounded). Shares use the 356 records with abstracts as denominator; counts are lower bounds. Retrieved 2026-11-23, source https://api.crossref.org/journals/0266-7215/works.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical by method words: "survey" 126 (35.4%), "panel/longitudinal" 85 (23.9%), "administrative data/register/census" 56 (15.7%), "regression" 47 (13.2%), "experiment" 47 (13.2%), against "conceptual" 2 (0.6%). "theory" appears in 78 abstracts (21.9%) but also in empirical framing. The journal states its mission as research that "combines analytical theory and stringent empirical analysis" (https://web.archive.org/web/20260519234235/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/about, copy dated 2026-05-19) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Quantitative dominates by method words: "survey" 35.4%, "causal" 22 (6.2%), "quantitative" 4 (1.1%), against "interview" 5 (1.4%), "qualitative" 3 (0.8%), "ethnograph-" 0, "participant observation/fieldwork" 0, "mixed methods" 0. The replication policy distinguishes "statistical or computational methods" from qualitative data (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18). The journal's own about page quotes a testimonial calling it a leading journal of "empirical, quantitative and comparative studies" (copy dated 2026-05-19); a testimonial is not an editorial statement |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Not scored from counts. The guidelines say the journal publishes original research "in all fields of Sociology" (about page, copy dated 2026-05-19). Topic words: "inequality" 83 (23.3%), "gender" 90 (25.3%), "immigration" 49 (13.8%), "stratification/mobility" 52 (14.6%), "organizations/firms/labor market" 77 (21.6%), "life course" 23 (6.5%) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One stated orientation: the journal's mission is "to foster sociological research that combines analytical theory and stringent empirical analysis to contribute to a cumulative and generalising body of knowledge on the social world" (https://web.archive.org/web/20260519234235/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/about, copy dated 2026-05-19; the same sentence appears on the why-submit page, copy dated 2025-07-02).
- **What kind of engagement?** The editors reserve the right to decide whether papers fall within the scope of the journal and "to not accept papers for peer review" that clearly do not meet its standards and publication profile (https://web.archive.org/web/20250918094256/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions, copy dated 2025-09-18).
- **Article type and length**: original research articles of usually about 8,000 words including endnotes and references, excluding tables and figures; Data Briefs; Comments and Replies (same copy; see Format).
- **Replication condition**: for submissions received from 2025-01-01, authors of articles relying on statistical or computational methods must deposit a replication package as a condition of publication, to be supplied at conditional acceptance with a statement at first submission that the standard is met or an exemption is claimed; qualitative researchers are not required to submit one (same copy).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions or how many are declined before review; SciRev lists no immediate-rejection figure (https://scirev.org/journal/european-sociological-review/, retrieved 2026-11-23).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01-05 to 2026-11-19 whose title or abstract matches the regex listed in the AI-Research Notes; the denominator is the 356 records with an abstract (382 records in all; counts are lower bounds). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement or a count that is clearly dominant. The scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows were written for psychology and the humanities; where a row does not fit sociology it says so, and four rows were added.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | "experiment" 47 (13.2%); title-only 33 of 382 records. The word covers field experiments, factorial surveys and natural experiments (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcab043, https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcab001), not only laboratory work; "causal" 22 (6.2%) |
| Quantitative survey / observational (added row) | 4 | Clearly dominant count: "survey" 126 (35.4%), "panel/longitudinal" 85 (23.9%), "administrative data/register/census" 56 (15.7%), "regression" 47 (13.2%), "quantitative" 4 (1.1%). Editorial statements: the mission names "stringent empirical analysis", and the replication rule applies to "statistical or computational methods" (about page copy dated 2026-05-19; guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "interview" 5 (1.4%), "qualitative" 3 (0.8%). The replication policy names qualitative data (interviews, participant observation) as exempt and encourages archiving them, so qualitative work is anticipated by the rules (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18) |
| Ethnography and fieldwork (added row) | 0 | "ethnograph-" 0, "participant observation/fieldwork" 0 of 356 abstracts |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph-" 0 of 356 abstracts. The row is a poor fit for this venue: no sociology-specific evidence was sought beyond the count |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | By the convention, "theory" 78 (21.9%) scores 3, but that overstates pure theory work because the word appears in empirical framing; "conceptual" alone 2 (0.6%) would score 1. The aims pair "analytical theory" with empirical analysis. Treat as 1-3 |
| Mixed methods | 0 | "mixed methods" 0 of 356 abstracts |
| Comparative-historical / archival (added row) | 2 | "historical/archival" 10 (2.8%), "comparative-historical" 0 |
| Computational / text-as-data (added row) | 1 | "computational/text/ML" 3 (0.8%); the replication policy names "computational methods" |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | "meta-analysis" 0, "systematic review" 0. The row is a poor fit for this venue and is not evidence of rejection |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. In the 356 abstracts (abstract-only text; an independent recount on title plus abstract gave 301, 258 and 43 for the three counts, so the counts depend on that scope), 300 (84.3%) contain I, my, we or our (capitalised forms included); 258 contain "we" or "We"; 38 contain "I" or "my" (Crossref, regexes in notes; "our" can also be a generic plural, so this measures first-person wording, not necessarily a single author's voice). Examples seen in the first words of recent abstracts: "I exploit the case of a survey interview" (https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcaa069), "In this article, I evaluate" (https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcab027), "We analyse these incidents at the district level" (https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcaa055), "We address open questions" (https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcaa056); impersonal openings: "This paper investigates disparities" (https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcag044), "This study revisits that claim" (https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcag037). The guidelines say only that own work must be cited in wording that does not identify the author |
| **Expected density** | Length about 8,000 words including endnotes and references, excluding tables and figures; abstract 200 words or fewer (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18). No page-length statistics were taken |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Not more than 200 words, plus keywords and a 50 to 100 word biography per author (same copy) |
| **Writing style notes** | Format-free submission at first submission; author-date citations in parentheses, e.g. "(Gans, 1962)"; endnotes rather than footnotes; no more than two levels of subheadings; English only; the editors advise asking "would I enjoy reading and reviewing a manuscript formatted in this way?" (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18) |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author counts over the 356 abstract-bearing records (2021-2026): 80 single-author (22.5%), 121 two authors, 98 three, 31 four, 12 five, 5 six, 2 seven, 4 eight, one each with 9, 11 and 14 authors (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0266-7215/works, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No ethics-approval or IRB statement requirement on the ESR guidelines page (searched for "IRB", "institutional review", "informed consent", "ethics committee", "ethical approval", "human subjects": 0 hits outside HTML comments; https://web.archive.org/web/20250918094256/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions, copy dated 2025-09-18). The OUP publication-ethics page says journals publishing human-subject studies should ensure privacy is not infringed and that authors may be asked for evidence of ethical or legal approval (https://web.archive.org/web/20241001130642/https://academic.oup.com/pages/authoring/journals/preparing_your_manuscript/ethics, copy dated 2024-10-01) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are a minority: 80 of the 356 abstract-bearing Crossref records for 2021-2026 (22.5%; https://api.crossref.org/journals/0266-7215/works, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The title page asks for each author's institutional affiliation and contact details and each author's short biography may list affiliations and career history; no independent-scholar rule found (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | A Data Availability Statement is required for papers submitted on or after 2022-09-05. For submissions from 2025-01-01, a replication package (code and, where legal and ethical, data) is a condition of publication for statistical or computational work; it is due at conditional acceptance, but authors must say at first submission whether they meet the standard or claim an exemption; where data cannot be shared the statement must explain why and code is still required; qualitative researchers are not required to submit a package (https://web.archive.org/web/20250918094256/https://academic.oup.com/esr/pages/General_Instructions, copy dated 2025-09-18) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind: names, contact details, acknowledgements and funding go on a separate title page and supplementary files must be anonymous (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18). Posting the pre-submission version is allowed by OUP policy (copy dated 2026-11-02), which can reveal authorship |
| **AI use** | See AI Policy: OUP requires disclosure of AI use in cover letter and Methods or Acknowledgements; no journal-specific text found |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; Read and Publish agreements exist; APC unverified (OpenAlex lists 5323 dollars); see Open Access |
| **Authorship** | All listed authors must have contributed significantly and approved the final version; "ghost writing" is prohibited; author-order changes after submission need written approval of all authors; CRediT roles are encouraged (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: usually about 8,000 words including endnotes and references; longer papers are published but reviewers are asked whether the contribution justifies the length (Format; Peer Review; guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18).
- **Language**: the editors will for the time being only consider papers written in acceptable English, and language quality is the authors' sole responsibility (Format).
- **Anonymisation**: double-blind review requires anonymous manuscripts and supplementary files (Peer Review; Practical Concerns).
- **Replication package**: for statistical or computational work submitted from 2025-01-01, a replication package is a condition of publication, and the manuscript must state at first submission whether the standard is met or an exemption is claimed (Data transparency row, Framing Requirements).
- **Data availability statement**: required in every article (Data transparency row).
- **Parallel submission**: articles must not be under consideration elsewhere (guidelines copy dated 2025-09-18).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; the live guidelines page could not be read directly.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: SciRev authors report a 4.7-month first review round and 9.1 months total handling for accepted manuscripts (35 reviews, author-reported; Review Cycle Time). No journal-reported turnaround figure was found. After acceptance, the median to publication was 40 days in 2025 (publisher-reported).
- **Scope screen**: the editors may decline to send papers for review that clearly do not meet standards or profile (Desk Rejection Rate row); no rate is published.
- **Replication work**: preparing a documented replication package (code, readme, data version description) is an extra step for quantitative papers (Data transparency row).
- **Open access cost**: the OpenAlex-listed APC is 5323 dollars, unverified; accepted manuscripts can be shared immediately only on a personal webpage, with repository deposit after a 12-month embargo (Open Access; Preprint Policy).
- **Reviewer difficulty (author-reported)**: SciRev lists reviewer-comment difficulty 3.8 of 5 from 35 reviews (Reviewer Pool Characteristics).

### Best Suited For

- Quantitative sociology using survey, panel, register or experimental data: "survey" 35.4%, "panel/longitudinal" 23.9%, "administrative/register/census" 15.7%, "experiment" 13.2% of abstracts, and the mission text on "stringent empirical analysis" (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work on stratification, family, gender, migration and labour markets: "gender" 25.3%, "inequality" 23.3%, "immigration" 13.8%, "stratification/mobility" 14.6% of abstracts, and the top OpenAlex topics (Orientation, Subject Density).
- Cross-national or comparative designs: the most-cited recent records include a cross-national harmonised field experiment and a multi-country field experiment (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Authors who can release code and documentation: the replication rule (Practical Concerns).
- Data-source papers: the journal runs a Data Briefs section (Format).

### Not Recommended For

- Qualitative, ethnographic or mixed-methods work as the main contribution: "interview" 1.4%, "qualitative" 0.8%, "ethnograph-" 0, "mixed methods" 0 of 356 abstracts (Methodological Preferences). The replication rule exempts qualitative data, so such papers are not excluded by the rules; the counts show they are rare here.
- Purely conceptual or theoretical papers: "conceptual" 0.6% of abstracts (Methodological Preferences); the mission text pairs theory with empirical analysis.
- Authors needing a journal-reported turnaround or acceptance rate: none was found (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
- Authors who cannot supply a replication package for statistical work (Hard Blockers).
- Papers on decolonial or Indigenous themes, or AI: 0 of 356 abstracts match (Sensitive Topics); absent, not rejected.
